- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and prices are trending upward, model often underestimates; adjust up by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is near recent mean, model often drifts toward extremes; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = 0.8×prior + 0.2×true recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; dampen forecast volatility by 15–20% relative to sentiment-driven volatility.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., bullish → bearish → bullish), model often misreads trend; use 3-period sentiment average to smooth forecast bias.
